title: 元知识详解：预测与校准 — Day 68

questions.question: 一位分析师上个月有一次报「90% 会发生」的事最后没发生。按校准的标准，该如何评价他？
options: 一次落空说明不了什么，要看他所有「90%」的兑现率
这次失误已证明他过度自信，应把今后的置信度一律下调
只要他多数预测的方向说对了，就说明他校准良好
说明他应改为更多地报 50%，这样才不会再错
questions.explanation: 校准看的是频率对齐：所有「90%」里只兑现六成才是系统性过度自信，一次落空可能只是那剩下的一成。永远报 50% 虽然能完美校准，却不提供任何决策信息，布莱尔评分会惩罚这种躲闪。
questions.question_en: Last month an analyst said one event was 90% likely, and it didn't happen. By the standard of calibration, how should we judge them?
options_en: One miss proves little; check whether about 90% of everything they called at 90% came true
This miss proves overconfidence, so all their future confidence levels should be lowered
As long as most of their calls pointed the right way, they are well calibrated
It shows they should say 50% more often so they stop being wrong
questions.explanation_en: Calibration is about frequencies: only if their 90% calls come true about 60% of the time is there systematic overconfidence; a single miss may be the expected one in ten. Always saying 50% can be perfectly calibrated but carries no decision value, and the Brier score penalizes that hedging.

questions.question: 甲对每件事都报 50%，从不「翻车」；乙敢报 85% 或 15%，偶尔栽大跟头。按布莱尔评分的思路，通常谁更好、为什么？
options: 乙更好：评分也奖励分辨力，甲虽安全却没提供可用信息
甲更好：完美校准是好预测的唯一标准，甲做到了
甲更好：评分只惩罚自信地错，甲从未自信地错过
乙更好：评分只看你敢不敢把话说死，与结果对错其实无关
questions.explanation: 布莱尔评分可拆成校准、分辨力和事件固有不确定性。永远躲在 50% 能校准却毫无分辨力；评分同时惩罚过度自信和这种懦弱。它当然看结果——报 90% 却没发生要罚 0.81。
questions.question_en: Forecaster A always says 50% and never 'blows up'; forecaster B commits to 85% or 15% and occasionally takes a big hit. By the logic of the Brier score, who usually does better, and why?
options_en: B: the score also rewards resolution, and A, though safe, provides no information anyone can act on
A: perfect calibration is the sole criterion of a good forecast, and A achieves it
A: the score only punishes confident errors, and A never makes one
B: the score only rewards boldness, regardless of whether forecasts come true
questions.explanation_en: The Brier score decomposes into calibration, resolution and inherent uncertainty. Hiding at 50% can be calibrated but has zero resolution, and the score penalizes that timidity as well as overconfidence. It certainly depends on outcomes — saying 90% for something that doesn't happen costs 0.81.

questions.question: 给一个新技术项目排期，按参考类预测的做法，第一步应该是什么？
options: 先把需求拆解到最细，逐项估工时后加总
先查同类项目实际耗时的基率，再按本次情况温和调整
先找一个与本项目最相似的成功案例，照它的实际工期来排
先听最了解项目的核心成员的判断，以他为准
questions.explanation: 外部视角先锚在同类事件的历史统计上，再用眼前证据微调，顺序不能颠倒。自下而上拆解是内部视角，越投入越系统性乐观；只挑一个成功案例则丢掉了同类项目的失败分布。
questions.question_en: When scheduling a new technical project using reference class forecasting, what should come first?
options_en: Break the requirements down to the finest level, estimate each piece and add them up
Look up the base rate of how long comparable past projects actually took, then adjust modestly for specifics
Find the single most similar successful project and copy its timeline
Defer to the judgment of the team member who knows the project best
questions.explanation_en: The outside view anchors on the historical statistics of the reference class and only then adjusts for case-specific evidence; the order matters. Bottom-up decomposition is the inside view, which grows more optimistic the more invested you are, and picking one success story discards the distribution of failures.
